marta: Heads-up: pushed new decode-rate classifier thresholds to staging. Need quick sanity check before canary. TL;DR we split into 3 decode-rate buckets: slow (<20 tok/s), mid (20-70 tok/s), fast (>70). Also adjusted prompt-length buckets: short <64, med 64-512, long >512. Results look promising but KV hit-rate dropped for long+fast. Details below.

leo: where are the perf numbers? can you paste the staging traces + p95 latency?

marta: Staging profile: p50/p95/p99 per bucket
```
short-fast: 12/28/45ms
med-mid: 35/68/120ms
long-fast: 150/380/820ms
```
kv-hit-rate for long-fast fell from 0.78 -> 0.62 after classifier changes. token-budget targets currently: short 256, med 512, long 2048

sanjay: kv-hit-rate drop likely from mis-bucketing: long prompts that share prefixes got classified as 'fast' because decode-rate estimator uses sliding window. We saw per-request burst decode-rate noise. Could we smooth with EWMA over first 32 tokens?

marta: good call. I tried EWMA alpha=0.2 and re-ran — kv-hit now 0.71 and p95 long-fast -> 330ms. tradeoff: slower detection of true fast streams, small p50 regressions on short-fast.

jen: :thinking_face: what's the admission policy? are we still allowing token-budget steal between pools?

leo: current admission: token_budget_target per bucket with soft-redistribution: if pool not filled within 12ms, admission will borrow up to 15% from adjacent slower bucket. That borrowing is causing the long-fast mixes.

marta: I proposed toggling soft-redistribution to 0% for canary for 12 hours to isolate. Also want to try kernel hint: prefer grouped attention kernel for long+med buckets. Patch in diff: `runtime.batch.classifier.decode_rate.window=32` and `runtime.batch.admission.soft_redistribution=0`

ci-bot: ci: e2e tests for batching-classifier passed (unit=42, smoke=8). Benchmark job id: bmk-2026-03-18-1123

sanjay: Two quick experiments: A) EWMA alpha 0.2 + soft_redistrib=0 B) EWMA alpha 0.35 + soft_redistrib=10, run 4-hour canary A/B with 10% traffic each. Metric hooks: kv_hit_rate, p95, token_cost_per_1k. Also track prefix-sharing ratio.

jen: Agree. Add rollback criteria: if kv_hit_rate drops >0.05 or p95 increases >20% for any bucket -> rollback. Notify #eng-oncall on threshold.

leo: I'll open canary with runway script. Command:
```
./canary/run.sh --config staging-classifier-A --traffic 0.1 --duration 4h
``` 
I'll tag you when started @marta @sanjay

marta: Thanks. After canary we should run a microbenchmark reproducing prefix-heavy long-fast cases (20k traces). I have a generator skr: `tools/gen_prompts.py --mode prefix-heavy --len 800 --rate 120`
